name: La Pèira Terrasses du Larzac La Pèira 2016
text:
## La Pèira Terrasses du Larzac La Pèira 2016

**The story.** La Pèira was founded in 2004 by an unlikely winemaker: [Rob Dougan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Dougan), the Sydney-born composer best known for "Clubbed to Death (Kurayamino Variation)", the music made famous by the 1999 film [The Matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Dougan)). His wife was born in [Montpellier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montpellier), which first drew him to the region, and he was attracted by its [Occitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_language) past and "its difficulties in being embraced by France". His family had farmed sheep and cattle in Australia on a huge scale, but not grapes. He describes La Pèira as a site that existed "for hundreds and hundreds of years" before his family arrived: many of the vines were planted before he was born, and he sees their role as simply paying tribute to the place ([La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)). Within a few years, critics were ranking it among France's best: Jeb Dunnuck has called it "one of the best in France" ([La Pèira](https://la-peira.com/la-peira/)).

**The land: the Terrasses du Larzac.** La Pèira is in the Terrasses du Larzac, at the foot of the [Larzac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larzac), a limestone [karst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karst) plateau in the south of the Massif Central between Millau and [Lodève](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lod%C3%A8ve), in the [Hérault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9rault), where sheep traditionally give milk for [Roquefort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roquefort) cheese ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larzac); [see the area from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=La+P%C3%A8ira,+Terrasses+du+Larzac,+H%C3%A9rault,+France&t=k)). Despite the name, Dougan explains, "terrasses" here is a geological term: the vineyards sit on what the wine writer Andrew Jefford calls the "tenderloin", a flattish bench of rock and gravel left by ancient rivers; the American critic David Schildknecht politely called it "only mildly tilted". The estate works about 14 hectares in three plots right around the cellar, all with the same aspect and soil. Even so, Dougan is puzzled that Syrah from two plots a few hundred metres apart never tastes the same ([La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)).

**The wine: La Pèira.** The flagship comes entirely from one plot, the Bois de Pauliau, and is mainly [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) with [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache); only about 3,000 bottles are made a year ([La Pèira](https://la-peira.com/la-peira/)). The vines are short-pruned and worked by hand or tractor, without chemicals. In the cellar, all the grapes are destemmed and left in a cold soak with their skins for several weeks before fermentation begins slowly, with no punching down: "Everything's done very gently and slowly". The wine is aged in barrels of several sizes and ages from different coopers, so no single barrel style steers it ([La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)). For 2016 the Wine Advocate gives the blend as 70% Syrah, 25% Grenache and 5% [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), aged two years in 40% new oak; the share of Grenache dropped because Grenache struggled in the region that year ([La Pèira blog](https://blog.la-peira.com/2018/10/03/la-peira-2016-up-with-the-finest-vintages-of-this-cuvee-and-a-candidate-for-perfection-97-99-100-jeb-dunnuck/); [La Pèira](https://la-peira.com/la-peira/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Languedoc-Roussillon vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/languedoc-roussillon) describes 2016 as warm and sunny throughout the summer with usefully fresh nights. Some areas lacked rain, giving smaller yields of concentrated juice, but the dry conditions kept disease away, and quality is generally good, with high flavour intensity. The estate adds that the summer was said at the time to be the driest since 1944, and that quality was especially high in appellations farthest from the sea, like the Terrasses du Larzac ([La Pèira](https://la-peira.com/la-peira/)).

**What the critics say for 2016.** As published on the estate's own vintage page and blog ([La Pèira](https://la-peira.com/la-peira/); [blog](https://blog.la-peira.com/2018/10/03/la-peira-2016-up-with-the-finest-vintages-of-this-cuvee-and-a-candidate-for-perfection-97-99-100-jeb-dunnuck/)), so treat them as the estate's selection:
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 97 to 99.** "Up with the finest vintages of this cuvée and a candidate for perfection": black raspberries, [garrigue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrigue), olives, [lavender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavandula) and truffles; full-bodied, with terrific mid-palate depth and sweet, polished tannins, yet remarkable elegance and purity. Two decades of life.
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95** (bottle; 95 to 97 from barrel). Some caramel and toast from the oak, accenting rich dark fruit; full-bodied and ripe, "almost syrupy" in concentration, with cola, plum and baking spice and a soft dusting of tannin on a long finish. "Impressive stuff that should drink well for a decade or more."
- **[Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson): 17.5/20.** Heady, intense and already complex, enormously ripe and concentrated yet beautifully refined, with the smoothest tannins; "Really very classy indeed", exceptionally long and pure without excess heat. "This is great winemaking."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 94.7** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2023 to 2033; the Wine Advocate expected a decade or more of good drinking and Dunnuck two decades. So it is in its prime now. Expect dark berries, olive, garrigue and smoky, savoury notes, the oak by now absorbed. Decant 1 to 2 hours ahead.

**Serving.** Serve at about 16 to 17°C, a little below room temperature, in a large glass; [decant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation) it ahead, since a rich Syrah like this opens with air.

**Food.** The Larzac is sheep country, so lamb is the natural match: a slow-roasted shoulder with garlic and thyme, or a leg with [herbes de Provence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbes_de_Provence). [Cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet), a beef [daube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daube) or [wild boar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar) stew would also suit, and a wedge of [Roquefort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roquefort), made from Larzac sheep's milk, is a fun local pairing to end with. I'd avoid delicate fish.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists La Pèira, and with about 3,000 bottles a year it is scarce. Jancis Robinson noted at the time that Berry Bros & Rudd used to list it and that UK stockists were few ([La Pèira](https://la-peira.com/la-peira/)), so look for it at auction and with specialist merchants.

**From the history books**
- **A troubled land.** The [Albigensian Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensian_Crusade) (1209–1229), launched by Pope Innocent III against the [Cathars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catharism) of Languedoc, brought the region under the French crown and diminished its distinct culture, part of the "troubled" history Dougan says drew him here ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensian_Crusade); [La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)).
- **Sixty owners.** Reading the property records, Dougan found some sixty previous owners listed, each of whom had planted or cared for the vineyard, which made him feel he was "coming upon a found object" ([La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)).
- **The vines before Rob.** The first vineyard he bought had been planted over the previous fifty years with local [Cinsault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinsaut) and [Carignan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carignan) and the Rhône's Syrah, Grenache and Mourvèdre; whites include [Viognier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viognier), [Roussanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roussanne), [Marsanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsanne) and [Clairette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clairette_blanche) ([La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)).

**Curious details**
- **From The Matrix to the vineyard.** Dougan's 1995 single, "Clubbed to Death", became famous through The Matrix soundtrack in 1999, and he also co-remixed U2's "Numb" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Dougan)).
- **Two barrels, two schools.** Dougan once bottled a 100% Mourvèdre from just one barrel and left its twin aside: the same wine had developed so differently in two barrels it was "like it had gone to two different schools" ([La Pèira interview](https://la-peira.com/interview-with-rob-dougan)).
- **Fishing, not engineering.** He says he didn't come to wine to make a particular style: "It's like fishing. You put your rod in the ocean and you see what comes up."
- **Never mixed.** The second wine, Las Flors, comes entirely from the neighbouring Belle Fiolle plot, and no Belle Fiolle grapes have ever gone into La Pèira.
